title: The Sun is a star
keyIdea: The Sun is a star: a huge ball of hot, glowing gas that makes its own light and heat. It is the closest star to Earth. It looks much bigger and brighter than the other stars only because it is so much nearer; many stars are bigger. The Sun is at the centre of our solar system, and all eight planets, Earth too, orbit around it. The Moon and the planets make no light of their own; they shine because they reflect sunlight.
familyTip: On a clear night, find the brightest dots together and ask: is it a star or a planet? Planets usually shine with a steady light, while stars twinkle. Then hold a torch close and far away across a dark room. It is the same torch, but it looks smaller and dimmer when it is far away, just like other suns.

visual.caption: Star, or not a star? Drag each one to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Sirius, the brightest star at night

lab.caption: Flagship lab: fly away from the Sun, compare real star sizes, sort what makes light, put the Sun in the middle, and time starlight.

kid: The Sun is a star. It is a huge ball of very hot gas. It makes its own light and heat.
The Sun looks big and bright because it is close to us. Other stars are suns too, but they are very, very far away. So they look like tiny dots. Some of them are even bigger than our Sun.
The Sun is in the middle of our solar system. The Earth and the other 7 planets travel round it. One trip round the Sun takes the Earth one year.
The Moon and the planets do not make light. They shine because light from the Sun bounces off them.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. This builds towards the Year 5 Earth and space unit in the National Curriculum in England: describe the movement of the Earth, and other planets, relative to the Sun in the solar system, and describe the Sun, Earth and Moon as approximately spherical bodies. Key words: star, Sun, solar system, planet, orbit, light source, reflect, distance, light year.

The Sun is an ordinary star, a G-type main-sequence star, about 150 million km away; its light takes about 8 minutes to reach us. The next nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light years away, so its light takes just over 4 years. Apparent size and brightness fall off with distance, which is why the Sun dominates our sky. Sirius is about 1.7 times as wide as the Sun and Betelgeuse is hundreds of times wider.

Common mistakes: thinking the Sun is not a star because it looks so different; thinking it is the biggest or brightest star; thinking the Sun goes round the Earth because it seems to cross the sky; calling the Moon or Venus (the 'evening star') a star; and thinking stars disappear in the daytime, when the bright sky only hides them.

In the lab your child flies away from the Sun until it shrinks to a dot like the others, compares three stars at their real sizes, sorts six sky objects into light makers and reflectors, drags the Sun to the centre of the solar system and runs a year, then times the light from the Sun and two other stars.

choices: A star, the closest one to Earth
practice.hint: Does the Sun make its own light?
practice.explain: The Sun makes its own light and heat, so it is a star. It is the star closest to Earth.

practice.prompt: Why does the Sun look so much bigger than the stars at night?
choices: It is much closer to us
It is the biggest star of all
Night stars are only lights in the sky
practice.hint: Think of a torch near you and a torch far away.
practice.explain: The Sun is far nearer than any other star. Things look smaller and fainter the farther away they are.

practice.prompt: The Earth takes 1 year to go once round the Sun. How many times does it go round in {n} years?
practice.hint: One trip round the Sun takes one year.
practice.explain: One orbit takes a year, so in {n} years the Earth goes round the Sun {n} times.

practice.prompt: Which of these makes its own light?
practice.hint: Which one is a ball of hot, glowing gas?
practice.explain: Stars make their own light. The Moon and Mars only reflect light from the Sun.

practice.prompt: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach us. How many minutes would {n} trips like that take?
practice.hint: Each trip takes about 8 minutes. Multiply by the number of trips.
practice.explain: {n} × 8 minutes = {=8*n} minutes. Light from any other star takes years, not minutes.

pool.prompt: What is at the centre of our solar system?
pool.hint: What do all the planets travel round?
pool.explain: The Sun is at the centre. All 8 planets, including Earth, orbit it.

pool.prompt: Sam says the Sun cannot be a star because stars are tiny. What would you tell him?
choices: Stars only look tiny because they are far away
He is right, the Sun is not a star
Stars are smaller than the Moon
pool.hint: How does a torch look when it is far away?
pool.explain: Stars are huge, but they are so far away that they look like dots. The Sun is a star that is close.

pool.prompt: Venus is very bright in the evening sky. What is it?
pool.hint: People call it the evening star, but does it make its own light?
pool.explain: Venus is a planet. It shines because sunlight reflects off it, even though people call it the evening star.

pool.prompt: Why can we see the Moon shining at night?
pool.hint: Does the Moon make light, or does it bounce light?
pool.explain: The Moon makes no light. We see sunlight that bounces off its surface.

pool.prompt: Are there stars in the sky in the daytime?
choices: Yes, but the bright sky hides them
No, they move behind the Sun
pool.hint: Is it hard to see a torch in bright sunshine?
pool.explain: The stars are still there. Sunlight makes the sky so bright that their faint light is hidden.

pool.prompt: Is the Sun the biggest star?
choices: Yes, stars are all the same size
pool.hint: Does looking big mean being big?
pool.explain: Many stars are bigger. Betelgeuse is hundreds of times wider than the Sun. The Sun only looks biggest because it is nearest.

pool.prompt: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach us. Light from Proxima Centauri takes about 4 years. Which star is closer to Earth?
pool.hint: The shorter the trip, the closer the star.
pool.explain: Light from the Sun arrives in minutes, but light from Proxima Centauri takes years, so the Sun is far closer.

choices: Nothing, the Sun goes round the Earth
pool.hint: How many planets are in our solar system?
pool.explain: All 8 planets orbit the Sun. The Sun seems to cross our sky because the Earth spins.

pool.prompt: Ava is {n} years old. How many times has the Earth gone round the Sun since she was born?
pool.hint: Each trip of the Earth round the Sun takes one year.
pool.explain: One orbit takes one year, so in {n} years the Earth has gone round the Sun {n} times.

pool.prompt: Light from Proxima Centauri takes about 4 years to reach us. How long would light take from a star {n} times as far away?
pool.hint: Light goes at the same speed all the way, so twice as far takes twice as long.
pool.explain: {n} × 4 years = {=4*n} years. The farther a star is, the longer its light takes, and the smaller and fainter it looks.
